quotes.text: This further increases the pressure on Eliza to touch the glass.
The two plausible answers are for Eliza to touch the glass in the lower left-hand corner or the cup in the lower right-hand corner.

expected.note: The central problem of the book: Surround 5 and the chapter 4 run are this configuration; the ids are Surround 5's.

method: The figure was extracted from the F95 PDF with `pdfimages -png` (an embedded JPEG at 135 ppi; chapter 2's figures draw the table alone, 227-246 x 221-229 px, the frame nearly filling the image, with 'Henry' above it and 'Eliza' below it); the table's frame was found as the darkest column and row profiles of the image's left and right eighths and top and bottom quarters (tools/measure_figure.py, find_frame); each icon's bounding box was read from the clusters of pixels darker than grey level 200 (components, merged within 2 px) and, where the H arrow or a neighbouring icon touches an icon, from an ASCII dump of the region, taking the icon's own outline (the cup's rim row, the right edge of its handle and its bottom row; a spoon's bowl and handle; a fork's tines, crossbar and handle) and leaving the arrow out; the object's position is the centre of that box as a fraction of the frame's inner width and height, scaled to the 110 x 100 table (D-001, D-003). The silverware's orientation was read on the enlarged image (tines, blade and bowl at the top: `up`). Chapter 2's figures carry no E arrows, so `answers` is empty and French's expectation in words is the `expected` block (docs/problems.md 9).

uncertainty.note: One pixel is 0.51 units in chapter 2's figures (frames of 212-215 x 193-196 px, a tenth larger than chapter 5's); icon boxes are good to about 1 px, and the touched cup, which the H arrow overlaps, to about 2 px. Figure 2.11 is the configuration of Surround 5 and of the chapter 4 screen dumps; measured here it agrees with problems/surround-05.json to within 1.9 units in x and 2.3 in y over the thirteen objects (median 0.7; docs/problems.md 9).

notes: The knife stands under the H label and its blade touches the arrow; the knife (x 53-55) and the cup (rim row 42, handle to x 76, bottom row 48) were read on the dump.
review: Reviewed: fork, fork, knife, the touched cup (H), spoon, spoon on Henry's side; spoon, spoon, small glass, fork, fork, knife on Eliza's; the isolated cup lower right. French: the groups have the same number of objects and the same objects, not arranged the same way [F95 p. 30]; 'Take close note of this problem' [F95 p. 31]. Identical in layout to Surround 5 [F95 p. 118 (img)] and the chapter 4 dumps.
